name: Lidocaine
short: Local anesthetic that blocks sodium channels on primary afferents.
mechanism: Blocks **voltage-sensitive sodium channels** on primary afferent neurons, stopping nociceptive impulses from entering the CNS.

name: Clonidine
short: Nonselective α2 agonist (plus imidazoline); ER form approved for ADHD.
mechanism: A **direct-acting, nonselective α2 agonist** (α2A, α2B, α2C) that also binds **imidazoline** receptors. Postsynaptic α2A stimulation in the PFC strengthens the signal; α2B, α2C and imidazoline actions add **sedation and hypotension**. In the spinal cord it mimics descending noradrenergic pain inhibition.

facts.text: Approved for hypertension; only **controlled-release** clonidine is approved for ADHD. Guanfacine is 10× weaker at sedation/hypotension and 25× more potent on PFC function.
Reduces the **intensity** (autonomic symptoms) but not the duration of opioid withdrawal.

updates.title: A liquid clonidine for ADHD
updates.text: **Onyda XR** (clonidine ER oral suspension) was approved in May 2024 for ADHD from age 6, alone or with stimulants, dosed once daily at bedtime.
updates.source: Drugs.com approval history; Tris Pharma, May 29, 2024

name: Naloxone
short: μ-opioid antagonist that reverses placebo analgesia.
mechanism: Blocks **μ-opioid** receptors. Its ability to reverse placebo pain relief suggests placebo analgesia involves endogenous opioid release.

facts.text: Competitive μ antagonist that reverses opioid overdose and can precipitate withdrawal. (The book claims fentanyl cannot be reversed; it can, though larger or repeated doses may be needed.)
Combined with **buprenorphine**: inactive sublingually but blocks the high if the tablet is injected.

updates.title: Naloxone over the counter
updates.text: Narcan 4 mg nasal spray was approved for **over-the-counter** sale on March 29, 2023.

name: Cyclobenzaprine
short: Tricyclic muscle relaxant used second line for fibromyalgia.
mechanism: A **tricyclic** muscle relaxant; the book does not detail its pharmacology.

updates.title: Sublingual form approved for fibromyalgia
updates.text: Tonmya, a once-nightly sublingual cyclobenzaprine tablet, was approved for fibromyalgia in adults on August 15, 2025, the first new fibromyalgia drug in more than 15 years.
updates.source: FDA approval reported by Healio, August 15, 2025

name: Modafinil
short: A DAT inhibitor used with an SNRI as an “arousal combo.”
mechanism: Racemic wake-promoting agent acting mainly as a **DAT inhibitor**: weak affinity but high plasma levels give slow, sustained (6–8 h), incomplete DAT occupancy that raises **tonic** dopamine, then downstream **histamine** (TMN) and **orexin** release. Works even without orexin neurons.
uses: With an SNRI for residual **fatigue, low energy and poor concentration/alertness** in depression (arousal combo)

facts.text: Used for ancillary symptoms of **fibromyalgia** (see Chapter 9 table).
Possibly less powerful than stimulants in narcolepsy but with much lower abuse potential; often needs a second daily dose.
Also a DAT blocker: the more rapidly and completely the DAT is blocked, the more reinforcing a drug becomes.

name: Armodafinil
short: Wake-promoting agent used for fibro-fog and fatigue.
mechanism: The **R enantiomer** of modafinil: a DAT inhibitor with later peak, longer half-life and higher plasma levels 6–14 h after dosing, possibly avoiding a second daily dose.
uses: **Fibro-fog** and fatigue in fibromyalgia (as for cognitive dysfunction in depression)

name: Solriamfetol
short: Wake-promoting NDRI for narcolepsy and OSA.
mechanism: An **NE and DA reuptake inhibitor**: more potent than bupropion, less potent but more tolerable and **less abusable** than stimulants; short half-life wears off by bedtime.

name: Pitolisant
short: H3 autoreceptor antagonist for narcolepsy; not controlled.
mechanism: Blocks presynaptic **H3 autoreceptors**, disinhibiting **histamine release** to promote wakefulness.
uses: In testing for OSA sleepiness (at publication)

sideEffects.e: No known abuse potential; not a controlled substance

facts.text: About as effective as modafinil, perhaps less than stimulants.

updates.title: Pediatric approval
updates.text: Approved in June 2024 for excessive daytime sleepiness in children aged 6 and older with narcolepsy.

name: Caffeine
short: The world’s most used psychoactive drug: an adenosine antagonist.
mechanism: Blocks **adenosine** receptors. Adenosine (the “accountant” of fatigue) heterodimerizes its receptors with **D2** receptors and lowers their dopamine affinity; caffeine restores it, enhancing DA action.

name: Sodium oxybate (GHB)
short: Narcolepsy drug that enhances slow-wave sleep; abuse and diversion risk.
mechanism: **Full agonist at GHB receptors** and **partial agonist at GABA-B** receptors (antagonist when GABA is high, agonist when low). Increases **slow-wave sleep** and reduces cataplexy via GABA-B, so patients sleep so well at night they are less sleepy by day.
uses: **Cataplexy** and **excessive sleepiness** in narcolepsy (approved); reduces hypnagogic hallucinations and sleep paralysis
Severe, treatment-resistant **fibromyalgia** in expert hands (heroic cases)

sideEffects.e: “Date rape” misuse with alcohol (sedation, amnesia); abuse by athletes for growth hormone surge

updates.title: Once-nightly formulation
updates.text: Lumryz, an extended-release sodium oxybate taken once at bedtime, was approved in May 2023 for cataplexy or excessive daytime sleepiness in adults with narcolepsy.

facts.text: As GHB it is abused to get high and as a “**date rape**” drug; agonist at GHB and GABA-B receptors.

name: Oveporexton
short: First orexin receptor agonist (post-publication), for narcolepsy type 1.
mechanism: Not in the book: an oral **OX2 agonist** that replaces the missing orexin signal in narcolepsy type 1. Listed here because Chapter 10 explains why orexin loss causes narcolepsy.

updates.title: Approved for narcolepsy type 1
updates.text: Approved by the FDA on August 5, 2026 for adults with narcolepsy type 1; phase 3 trials improved sleepiness, cataplexy and quality of life; insomnia and urinary frequency were common.
